Verify size 0, getSize 0, getValue throws IndexOutOfBounds? Actually values list size zero; getValue(0) would cause index error. Maybe we test that values list empty and getValue not called.

2. testSimpleLongPositionMarkToMarket: series with 3 bars close prices 10, 20, 30. Create trading record: enter long at index 0 price 10 amount 1, exit at index 2 price 30. Use CashFlow with MARK_TO_MARKET and default open handling. Expect cash flow values: start with 1, after entry at index0 value still 1? Actually calculation multiplies by ratio at entry? So final cash flow at each bar should reflect growth: ratio = exitPrice / entryPrice = 30/10 = 3. For bars after entry, values multiplied accordingly. Expect value at index0 =1 (maybe multiplied later). At index1 (close 20) ratio = 20/10=2, so value at index1 =2. At index2 (exit) final ratio =3, value at index2 =3. So test getValue(0)=1, getValue(1)=2, getValue(2)=3.

3. testSimpleShortPositionMarkToMarket: series same, short entry at index0 price 30 (sell), exit at index2 price 10 (buy). For short, ratio formula: entryPrice *2 - exitPrice/entryPrice? Actually getIntermediateRatio for short: 2 - exitPrice/entryPrice. entryPrice =30, exitPrice=10 => 2 - (10/30)=2 - 0.3333 = 1.6667. For intermediate bar close 20: ratio =2 - (20/30)=2 - 0.6667=1.3333. So expect values: index0 =1, index1 =1.333..., index2 =1.666... Use Num tolerance.

4. testOpenPositionHandlingIgnore: create open position (entry only) and open handling IGNORE, finalIndex after entry. Expect cash flow unchanged (still 1) because ignored. Use CashFlow with OpenPositionHandling.IGNORE.

5. testEquityCurveModeRealized: Use realized mode where only realized profit applied at exit; ensure intermediate bars not multiplied. For long position, expect value at entry index 0 =1, after exit index2 = exit ratio (3) applied to range from entry to end. According to code: in realized case, after entry, they compute holdingCost etc, then multiplyRange from max(ratioIndex, windowStartIndex) to windowEndIndex with ratio. ratioIndex = endIndex (2). So only index2 multiplied. So value at index0 =1, index1 =1, index2=3. Test.

Include assertions using Num.doubleValue with tolerance.

But BaseTradingRecord.enter expects Num price, Num amount. Use series.numFactory().numOf(10) etc.
